title: Do Coding Agents Deceive Us? Detecting and Preventing Cheating via Capped Evaluation with Randomized Tests
abstract: arXiv:2606.07379v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: A growing failure mode in agent evaluation and training is that models can achieve high evaluation scores (e.g., test pass rates) by exploiting shortcuts instead of solving the intended task, making these scores deceptive. This makes evaluation scores unreliable as measures of true task-solving ability. We propose CapCode, a framework for constructing coding datasets with randomized tests whose best achievable non-cheating score is deliberately capped below 100%. This capped-score design gives evaluation scores a clearer interpretation: scores substantially above the cap are implausible and therefore provide evidence of cheating. To prevent cheating, we propose CapReward, a reward design based on the CapCode principle to discourage optimization beyond the cap. Experiments across multiple datasets show that CapCode detects cheating while preserving performance ranking of models, and CapReward reduces cheating behavior, yielding

translated_title: 编码智能体在欺骗我们吗？基于随机测试的封顶评估方法来检测与防止作弊
translated_abstract: 在智能体评估与训练中，一个日益严重的失效模式是：模型可以通过利用捷径而非真正解决预期任务来获得高评估分数（例如测试通过率），从而使这些分数具有欺骗性。这导致评估分数无法可靠地衡量模型真实的问题解决能力。我们提出了CapCode，这是一个用于构建带随机测试的编码数据集的框架，其中通过合法方式可达到的最高分数被刻意封顶在100%以下。这种封顶分数设计使评估分数具有更清晰的解释：显著超过上限的分数是不合理的，因此可以作为作弊的证据。为了防止作弊，我们提出了CapReward，这是一种基于CapCode原则的奖励设计，旨在抑制超出上限的优化行为。在多个数据集上的实验表明，CapCode能够在保持模型性能排名的同时检测作弊行为，而CapReward减少了作弊行为，从而……
tldr: 该论文提出CapCode框架与CapReward奖励设计，通过随机测试将合法可达分数刻意封顶在100%以下，使超出上限的分数成为作弊证据，从而检测并抑制编码智能体评估中的作弊行为。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes CapCode and CapReward, which deliberately cap the best achievable non-cheating score below 100% via randomized tests so that scores exceeding the cap provide evidence of cheating, thereby detecting and discouraging cheating behavior in coding agent evaluation.
